articles.title: ‘Couldn't stay silent’: Iranian footballers reveal why they refused to sing anthem before seeking asylum in Australia
articles.summary: Football News: Iranian footballers Atefeh Ramezanisadeh and Fatemeh Pasandideh have broken their silence over the protest that preceded their decision to seek asylum.
articles.body: Iranian footballers Atefeh Ramezanisadeh and Fatemeh Pasandideh have broken their silence over the protest that preceded their decision to seek asylum in Australia, confirming that their refusal to sing Iran's national anthem at the Women's Asian Cup was a deliberate act of defiance against Tehran.The two players, who abandoned the Iranian delegation after the tournament and remained in Australia, spoke publicly for the first time since claiming asylum. Their interview with Australia's 60 Minutes was broadcast on Sunday, shedding new light on a gesture that had sparked intense debate over whether the players were mourning their country amid the escalating conflict or protesting against Iran's government.For Ramezanisadeh, 34, and Pasandideh, 22, the message was clear: they were standing with protesters back home.‘We just wanted to stand with our people’Iran's women's team had remained silent when the national anthem was played before their opening match against South Korea on March 2. The refusal immediately drew criticism in Iran, with sections of the country's media branding the players as traitors.At the time, however, the team did not publicly explain the decision.The gesture came shortly after US and Israeli attacks on Iran began on February 28, leading some observers to interpret the silence as an act of mourning. Others saw it as an act of resistance against Tehran.Ramezanisadeh has now confirmed that the latter was the reason for her silence."We just wanted to stand with our people. I was scared at times, but I just tried to do what was right and say that no one should be killed just for protesting," Ramezanisadeh told Nine Network through an interpreter.She acknowledged the enormous personal risk involved in refusing to sing the anthem.Ramezanisadeh said her silence "could have meant any form of torture" for her."But at that moment, the only thing that gave me peace and a clear conscience was not singing it. I wanted to sing the anthem with pride and from my heart. But because of the situation in Iran, I really couldn't do it," she said.Pasandideh was equally direct about what motivated her."My people put their lives on the line and they were killed. Doing that was the absolute least we could do for them," Pasandideh said through an interpreter.Silence becomes a turning pointThe players' decision became even more significant after demonstrators in Australia called for the Iranian squad to be allowed to remain in the country rather than return home.The team eventually left Sydney on March 10, but the issue had already reached the highest levels of Australian politics.Australian Immigration Minister Tony Burke said the players had not been promised asylum when they made their decision."At that point, they had absolutely no information from us about the possibility of being able to stay," Burke said."The silence of itself was deeply significant," he added. "The reaction was the volcanic moment."The situation escalated further after then-US President Donald Trump publicly called for the Iranian players to be granted asylum and spoke to Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese about the issue.Albanese subsequently told Trump that four players and a team manager had accepted offers of humanitarian visas.Seven members of the Iranian delegation eventually accepted Australia's offer of asylum, but all except Ramezanisadeh and Pasandideh later changed their minds.The two women, meanwhile, decided to remain.‘I couldn't stay silent’Ramezanisadeh said the decision to stay in Australia came despite pressure from her parents, who urged her to return to Iran after receiving instructions from Iranian authorities."They tried to reassure me, saying: Nothing will happen to you. This is your home. You must return home.' But I told them my mind was made up and I was not coming back," she said.The decision has come at an enormous personal cost."Thinking that I might never be able to see my family again was heartbreaking, but I couldn't allow myself to be indifferent while so many young people were being killed by this regime. I couldn't stay silent, even though I miss my family so much," she added.Both players said they had not been in contact with their families in recent months, although they understood that their relatives had not been punished.Their decision to remain in Australia has also led to a new chapter in their football careers. Ramezanisadeh and Pasandideh now play for semi-professional club Wynnum Wolves in Brisbane and became Australian citizens in August.‘I don't want to put their lives in danger’Pasandideh said she had deliberately avoided asking her former teammates whether they wanted to return to Iran or whether they felt compelled to do so."We decided not to talk because I don't want to put their lives in danger," she said.Despite everything that has happened, her attachment to Iran remains strong."One of my biggest dreams is to be able to go back to Iran, but in different circumstances when the situation in Iran has changed and the people of Iran are happy and thriving. Then I will go back and see my family," she added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Champion’: Lionel Messi’s son Mateo captains Inter Miami Academy to Naples Cup title
articles.summary: Football News: Lionel Messi's son Mateo has taken another step in his budding football career, captaining the Inter Miami Academy to the Naples Cup title and giving .
articles.body: Lionel Messi's son Mateo has taken another step in his budding football career, captaining the Inter Miami Academy to the Naples Cup title and giving fans another glimpse of the youngster's footballing journey.Mateo, Messi's second son, was part of the Inter Miami Academy side that emerged victorious at the Copa Naples, with the achievement drawing attention across social media. The youngster was seen celebrating with the trophy after the triumph, proudly posing for photographs with the Copa Naples Cup, which carried the word 'champion'.Inter Miami's academy confirmed that its teams from the U-8 through U-12 age groups were competing in the 2026 Copa Naples, held at the Paradise Coast Sports Complex in Naples, Florida, on September 5 and 6.The title represents another memorable moment in Mateo's early football journey as he continues to develop within Inter Miami's youth setup.Mateo follows in Messi's footstepsMateo is the second of Lionel Messi and Antonela Roccuzzo's three sons. He will turn 11 on September 11, with his older brother Thiago 13 and younger brother Ciro eight.While his father has already established himself as one of the greatest players in football history, Mateo has gradually attracted attention for his own footballing ability.Videos of Mateo playing football have previously gone viral, with his skills, goals and competitive nature drawing comparisons with his famous father. His latest achievement, however, came not through a social-media clip but on the youth football circuit, where he helped lead Inter Miami Academy to a tournament title.Social media users were quick to celebrate the achievement after images of Mateo with the trophy circulated online. A video shared by Spanish publication Marca showed the youngster smiling for the cameras while holding the Copa Naples trophy.The Naples Cup triumph comes at an interesting time for the Messi family, with Lionel Messi himself having recently closed one major chapter of his career.A new chapter for the Messi familyMessi recently announced his retirement from international football after a remarkable 21-year career with Argentina. The decision came after Argentina's defeat to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, where Messi's side finished runners-up. Messi had said the decision was painful but necessary after he had given everything to the national side.The 39-year-old had previously fulfilled his biggest international ambition by leading Argentina to the 2022 World Cup title in Qatar.His international career may now be over, but Messi remains active at club level with Inter Miami. He recently assisted Casemiro's goal in a 2-2 draw against Atlanta United in his first club appearance after announcing his international retirement.That makes Mateo's Naples Cup success another intriguing development in a football family whose connection with the sport continues across generations.For now, Mateo remains at the beginning of his journey. But by captaining an Inter Miami Academy side to a tournament title and lifting the Naples Cup trophy, the youngster has added another notable achievement to a football story that is only just beginning.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: WNBA Analyst Slams FIBA World Cup Officials Over Missed Foul On Caitlin Clark
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark went scoreless while refs missed calls in a near-disaster for Team USA.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and officiating concerns go hand-in-hand. But things took a heavy turn when the same debate returned over the weekend in Berlin, when Team USA edged Italy 55-52 at the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup.

On September 6, 2026, Team USA's 31-game winning run in the FIBA Women's World Cup came dangerously close to ending. Before Sunday, the United States' closest game during its winning run was a 2010 victory over Australia, 83-75.

On Sunday, Italy led 50-49 with 3:21 left when the United States rallied in the fourth quarter, making Team USA's 55-52 escape the closest FIBA World Cup match for the Americans since their last loss in 2006.

The Sunday game did get physical eventually, with Clark struggling to find her flow. Sports Illustrated writer and WNBA analyst Robin Lundberg voiced his frustration with the bad officiating involving the Indiana Fever star guard by pointing to a specific play. In particular, Lundberg cited prior uncalled contact from Olbis Andre of Italy in the paint and a missed foul on Clark's arm on a late first-half drive to the basket as proof of subpar refereeing.

Speaking on his YouTube channel about the missed foul call on Clark during the Sunday game, Lundberg said, "There were some other questionable plays in the game, like Caitlin, you know, drove to the basket late at the end of the first half. This is a clear foul across the arm that wasn't called. It's the off arm there on that play. Wasn't called a foul. Didn't get to the free-throw line, obviously."

In the first quarter, there was another incident that heightened the suspense. With 2:03 left in the first quarter, play stopped while officials deliberated over a foul call involving Clark.

Clark approached to give her opinion, provoking a sideline reaction from Italy's head coach, Andrea Capobianco.

Later, Capobianco was seen yelling across the court, to which Clark responded, according to professional lip readers, "Stop complaining."

After falling behind 23-8, Italy shifted to a 2-3 zone halfway through the first quarter, and the outcome was instant. By halftime, they had trimmed the lead to 30-24 after going on a 16-7 run. In the third quarter, they maintained their momentum and briefly seized the lead.

Team USA was only able to shoot 29 percent from the field and 1-for-12 from three-point range because of Italy's defense. Furthermore, Team USA's 55-point total was its lowest World Cup score since defeating Australia 42-38 in 1967.

Nevertheless, Lundberg wasn't the only one who had concerns about the officiating. On X (formerly Twitter), sports commentator Jason Whitlock voiced a similar grievance.

Addressing the physicality of the Sunday game, Whitlock wrote, "That was a brutal game of basketball. If the refs are going to allow that level of physicality, there's a good chance we won't win."

Attributing Team USA's struggle to A'ja Wilson's absence and Italy's physicality, Whitlock added in the same post on X, "We missed A'ja Wilson today. The physicality eliminated CC and bothered (Breanna) Stewart throughout and slowed (Aliyah) Boston late. Ugly hoops."

Just days before the World Cup, Wilson was sidelined due to lingering back and health issues.

Although it's unlikely that they could play a worse game than that, Team USA has to improve overall and get more from Napheesa Collier, Breanna Stewart, and Clark.

Just like the final score, the individual stats for Team USA were equally rough. Clark had her first scoreless game from the field at any level of basketball, finishing 0-for-6 with one free throw. Before making her ninth shot, Stewart missed her first eight.

According to ESPN Insights , Stewart, Cooper, and Clark, who were all among the top seven scorers in the WNBA this season, shot 1-for-19 together with Kahleah Copper.

For the first time since the 2006 defeat to Russia, Team USA scored fewer than 70 points in a World Cup match on Sunday.

articles.title: Kylian Mbappe: Real Madrid forward says this could be good year to win Ballon d'Or
articles.summary: Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe says this could be a good year for him to win the Ballon d'Or for the first time.
articles.body:
Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe says this could be a good year for him to win the Ballon d'Or for the first time.

The 27-year-old scored 42 goals in 44 games for his club last season but they did not win any trophies.

He won the World Cup Golden Boot with 10 goals, taking his career tally at World Cups to a record 22 - although France finished fourth.

"I think when you play for Real Madrid, the best club in the world, people associate you with this award," he said.

"There are many people that speak about me and the Ballon d'Or. Of course I've made history in the most important competition. Maybe it's a good year for this but people can vote according to what they think."

He added: "I always think I'm the best [player in the world] but everyone has their own opinion.

"Maybe people think different ways. I don't think it's a discussion we need to have.

"Of course this year could be good for me to win the Ballon d'Or. But journalists vote."

The highest Mbappe has finished in the Ballon d'Or rankings is third in 2023, when he was a Paris St-Germain player.

Three players are given shorter odds with the bookmakers to win the Ballon d'Or, which will be awarded on 26 October.

England captain Harry Kane is odds-on to win, after a club-record 61 goals in 51 games for German double winners Bayern Munich last season. He also scored six times at the World Cup.

Lamine Yamal, who won La Liga with Barcelona and the World Cup with Spain, is second favourite - followed by his club and international team-mate Rodri, formerly of Manchester City.

Can Kane buck history and win Ballon d'Or?

'I really don't care' - Mbappe on PSG success after his exit

Mbappe, who started his career at Monaco, is the all-time top scorer for both PSG, with 256 goals in 308 games, and France, with 66 in 106.

He has netted 90 goals in 107 matches for Real Madrid but is yet to win a major trophy in two years at the Bernabeu.

On a personal basis, he has won eight consecutive league golden boots - six in Ligue 1 and two in La Liga - plus two in World Cups and another two in the Champions League.

He won the 2018 World Cup with France, but on a club level he has yet to win the Champions League.

PSG, who had never lifted the trophy before, have won it both seasons since Mbappe departed.

"I can't change it," he said of his former club's success without him.

"The truth is that I really don't care. I know how to analyse football, I know why.

"I don't know everything about football but I know more than most."

Speaking about Real's lack of recent trophies, he added: "My experience with Real Madrid says I shouldn't think too long-term because a lot can change.

"I want to think how I can be ready, to help my team to win the game and to start the Champions League in a good way."

articles.title: Mbappé y la rebelión de las estrellas contra el 'patrocinador obligado': una guerra que inició LeBron
articles.standfirst: El delantero francés apartó una botella de bebida isotónica durante la rueda de prensa previa de Champions en un gesto que recuerda al de Cristiano Ronaldo
articles.summary: El delantero francés apartó una botella de bebida isotónica durante la rueda de prensa previa de Champions en un gesto que recuerda al de Cristiano Ronaldo
articles.body: Hay gestos que duran un segundo y negocios que mueven millones. Kylian Mbappé protagonizó uno de esos esta mañana en Valdebebas. En la rueda de prensa previa al estreno del Real Madrid en la Champions frente al Inter, el delantero francés retiró del centro del plano una botella de Gatorade. Este gesto no es un capricho ni un arrebato de rebeldía higiénica. Es negocio. Mbappé, guardián de sus propios derechos de imagen y firmemente posicionado en contra de promocionar comida ultraprocesada o bebidas con alto contenido de azúcar, ha reabierto un melón histórico que comenzó en las canchas de la NBA. Una guerra fría en el deporte mundial donde las obligaciones comerciales de los torneos colisionan de frente con los imperios individuales de los atletas. Para entender el manotazo de Mbappé hoy en Valdebebas hay que viajar doce años atrás, a las Finales de la NBA de 2014. En el infierno de San Antonio, con el aire acondicionado roto a más de 32 grados, LeBron James cayó fulminado por calambres extremos en el primer partido del Miami Heat. Gatorade, patrocinador oficial de la NBA, olió la sangre y tuiteó con sorna: "Nosotros estábamos listos, el jugador que se acalambró no toma nuestro producto". El problema es que 'El Rey' era el rostro franquicia de Powerade (Coca-Cola). Aunque la marca borró el tuit y pidió perdón, la veda quedó abierta. Desde entonces, LeBron James instauró una costumbre en cada postpartido de la NBA: arrancar meticulosamente la etiqueta de Gatorade de las botellas obligatorias antes de responder a los micrófonos. Aquello resumía perfectamente la nueva realidad: la liga tenía sus patrocinadores y sus jugadores tenían los suyos. Y no siempre coincidían. El boicot se transformó en epidemia en el baloncesto estadounidense, una liga donde Gatorade inyecta millones (hasta el punto de dar nombre a la G League). Pero los contratos personales pesan más: Con el paso de los años, aquella batalla se convirtió casi en un pequeño género dentro de las ruedas de prensa de la NBA. Klay Thompson, uno de los rostros de BodyArmor (Coca-Cola), llegó a apartar las botellas de Gatorade de su espacio en los medios tirándolas con desprecio al suelo. Kawhi Leonard también protagonizó escenas similares, basando su discurso en la salud de los deportistas y añadiendo: "Los niños no necesitan estar tomando eso", en plena rueda de prensa. Stephen Curry, patrocinado por la marca de agua Oxigen, también ha sido visto apartando las botellas o haciendo gestos de desaprobación visual si se le encuadra junto al logotipo del rayo Esta 'guerra contra el patrocinador obligado' saltó del baloncesto a los mayores escenarios del fútbol internacional, dejando imágenes que cambiaron las políticas de marcas de las federaciones. Cristiano Ronaldo y el desplome de Coca-Cola (Eurocopa 2020) se convirtió en el momento más mediático de la historia del marketing deportivo. Durante la rueda de prensa previa al debut de Portugal en la Eurocopa (junio de 2021), Cristiano Ronaldo se sentó, miró con repulsión dos botellas de Coca-Cola (patrocinador oficial del torneo), las apartó del tiro de la cámara y, sosteniendo una botella de agua limpia, sentenció: "¡Agua! Coca-Cola, no". El gesto dio la vuelta al mundo en minutos. Coincidiendo con el desplome del mercado general en esa jornada, las acciones de Coca-Cola bajaron un 1.6%, perdiendo la compañía 4.000 millones de dólares en valor de mercado de forma momentánea durante esa franja horaria. Días después del incidente de CR7, Pogba retiró una botella de cerveza Heineken de su mesa de prensa. Al ser un musulmán devoto, Pogba no quería ser asociado visualmente con la promoción de bebidas alcohólicas (pese a que la botella en cuestión era la versión 0.0 sin alcohol). Este caos comercial obligó a la UEFA a emitir un comunicado de advertencia urgente a las selecciones nacionales, recordando que los ingresos de los patrocinadores son esenciales para el financiamiento de los torneos y amenazando con multas económicas a las federaciones si los jugadores seguían saboteando los productos en pantalla. Lo visto hoy en la rueda de prensa no pilla de sorpresa a quienes conocen la trayectoria del '10' blanco. Durante el Mundial de Qatar 2022, el delantero francés ejecutó un boicot sistemático a Budweiser, patrocinador oficial del premio MVP del partido. Mbappé posó repetidamente escondiendo el logotipo de la cervecera para cumplir con su estricta política de imagen: no asociar su nombre al alcohol, las apuestas o la comida rápida. Hoy, en la antesala de la Champions, la botella de Gatorade ha sido la última víctima del jugador que no solo domina el juego, sino también los encuadres de realización de televisión. Las marcas pagan fortunas por estar en esa mesa, pero las superestrellas globales mandan más que los logos. Una botella delante de un futbolista no es decoración: es una valla publicitaria de unos centímetros que puede aparecer en millones de fotografías, vídeos y redes sociales. Las marcas pagan por ese espacio, pero las grandes estrellas han aprendido que su cara también es un territorio propio. Mbappé pertenece a esa generación que ya no sólo juega al fútbol sino que también gestiona una marca, protege una imagen y decide hasta dónde quiere que llegue el patrocinio. El francés no necesitó levantar la voz ni convertir la rueda de prensa en una protesta. Le bastó con mover una botella. El producto salió del plano, y el delantero del Real Madrid volvió a recordarnos que el fútbol moderno también se juega ahí, en ese partido de logos, contratos y cámaras. A veces, para dejar claro quién decide, basta con apartar una botella.

articles.title: College Football Rankings Predictions for 2026 Week 2 AP and Coaches Polls
articles.summary: The Week 2 college football polls shouldn't look too much different from the preseason polls released in August.
articles.body:
The Week 2 college football polls shouldn't look too much different from the preseason polls released in August.

There were no surprise losses by Top 25 teams, although the Michigan Wolverines needed a last-chance Hail Mary to win their season opener.

The LSU Tigers and Ole Miss Rebels have the best arguments to move up in the rankings.

LSU opened the Lane Kiffin era with a 50-point performance at home against the Clemson Tigers.

Ole Miss kicked off life without Kiffin with a hard-fought win over the Louisville Cardinals in the only ranked matchup of the weekend.

Ole Miss, LSU With Best Cases To Move Up In Polls

Ole Miss and LSU own the best cases to make moves up the rankings after Week 1.

LSU produced arguably the most dominant performance of the weekend in its 51-10 thumping of Clemson in Baton Rouge.

The style of victory over a power-conference opponent might be enough to move LSU up into the top 10 from its No. 11 spot in the AP poll and No. 13 position in the Coaches poll.

Ole Miss had the best win of the weekend based on ranking since it played in the only Top 25 contest.

The Rebels won a shootout with Louisville on a last-second field goal.

Pete Golding's side was No. 9 in the preseason AP poll and No. 10 in the preseason Coaches poll. A move up of a spot or two could be warranted given the stature of the victory.

Louisville Has Case To Remain In AP Top 25

Louisville has an argument to remain in the AP Top 25, instead of dropping out from its No. 24 spot in the preseason poll.

The Cardinals put up a strong fight against a top-10 opponent in Ole Miss. They were tied with the SEC with one minute remaining.

The poll voters typically don't reward teams for losses, but in this case, Louisville might be able to hang on to its spot.

Jeff Brohm's side hung around against one of the top teams in the SEC and no one around it in the polls had an overly impressive weekend.

Clemson was the first team in the "others receiving votes" column of the preseason AP poll. The Tigers aren't deserving of any votes after Week 1.

The Florida Gators and Boise State Broncos were next in that column. Boise State suffered a hard-fought loss on the road at Oregon and Florida cruised against Florida Atlantic.

There's no clear replacement for Louisville in the AP poll. It likely won't appear in the Coaches poll, though, because it was unranked in that preseason rankings.

articles.title: Shrewsbury Town takeover by American consortium approved by EFL
articles.summary: Shrewsbury Town's long-running takeover saga is set to end after an American consortium is granted approval to buy the club.
articles.body:
Shrewsbury Town's long-running takeover saga is set to end after an American consortium was granted approval to buy the club.

The League Two club received written confirmation from the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) and the English Football League (EFL) on Monday confirming the as-yet-unidentified group's takeover had been approved.

The club said the new owner and principal investors will be announced "when we are able to do so".

"Now the regulatory processes have been successfully completed and approved, we move towards finalising the remaining documentation and concluding the takeover process as soon as possible," said a club statement. , external

"The chairman remains fully committed to finalising the transaction and ensuring a smooth takeover process."

Salop chairman Roland Wycherley put the club up for sale in 2024, but the collapse of potential takeovers had led frustrated supporter groups to send him an open letter demanding answers.

"Our detailed response to the open letter which we received on Sunday, 6 September, will be made after due consideration," the Shrewsbury statement added.

"We thank all of our supporters for their patience, and we will update you as soon as we are able to do so."

Though news of the takeover approval came just 24 hours after the open letter was sent, supporters' frustration had been brewing for some time following several failed attempts to purchase the Shropshire club.

Negotiations with an American buyer collapsed in March 2025, and six months later a second bid from a different party also fell through.

The club continued to report interest, but there had been no substantial news until June this year, when takeover terms were reported to have been agreed with an American consortium.

Once completed, the sale will bring an end to Wycherley's 30-year tenure as owner.

Town suffered relegation from League One in 2024-25 and needed a late-season revival under new boss Gavin Cowan to avoid dropping into the National League last term.

Analysis - BBC Radio Shropshire sports editor Nick Southall

This is as close as Shrewsbury has come to completing a takeover.

A different American businessman pulled out of the running a year and a half ago, before the Owners and Directors test.

So, this is a major milestone for the prospective owners to reach, and we could soon see a change which will bring chairman Roland Wycherley's 30-year spell at the top to an end.

Wycherley saved the club from bankruptcy in the 1990s and led the move to a brand-new stadium, leaving the iconic Gay Meadow.

There's no doubt football is a different beast now, and the prospect of new investment will come as a much-needed tonic, with Shrewsbury missing out on a number of key targets during the summer transfer window.

articles.title: After Lane Kiffin Saga, Ole Miss Win 'Felt Like a Therapy Session,' Says HC Pete Golding
articles.summary: While months have passed since Lane Kiffin's departure for LSU, Ole Miss may have still had some emotional baggage heading into Sunday's opener against Louisville.
articles.body:
While months have passed since Lane Kiffin's departure for LSU, Ole Miss may have still had some emotional baggage heading into Sunday's opener against Louisville.

The ninth-ranked Rebels prevailed over the No. 24 Cardinals thanks to a 48-yard field goal by Lucas Carneiro as time expired.

"It kind of felt like a therapy session," coach Pete Golding told reporters . "It didn't go very well for half of it, but it was awesome. It was a heavyweight fight. That was a good football team, and we got punched in the mouth a lot. We didn't always respond the right way."

New CFP Bracket Projections After Week 1 🔮

Ole Miss didn't bother with an interim tag and named Golding the permanent replacement for Kiffin prior to the College Football Playoff. The Rebels then reeled off two wins before losing in the Fiesta Bowl.

The unique circumstances behind Golding's promotion made it tough for everyone around the program to fully absorb the coaching change.

Everyone was fixated on competing for a national title, and the players may have had a point to prove to their old coach. Some assistants, most notably offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr., remained on the staff through the CFP before following Kiffin to Baton Rouge as well.

Sunday is when the Golding era really kicked off, and Kiffin's shadow continues to loom large.

"There's always going to be a piece for several years where — 'Oh that player was there when Lane was there, that's Lane's player,'" Golding told ESPN's David Hale . "If it works. If it doesn't, then Pete can't coach."

In another odd quirk, Golding is living in the house Kiffin owned after having bought it from his former boss.

No team is the finished product in Week 1, and that's especially true with how much rosters turn over now thanks to the transfer portal.

Sunday's victory wasn't totally convincing as Ole Miss allowed Louisville to gain 469 yards and threw away a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter. A win is a win, though, and the result should help Golding build confidence in himself as the leader on the sideline.

articles.title: Leicester City sink to new low in League One but can Russell Martin turn it around?
articles.summary: Leicester City find themselves sat 17th in League One after an embarrassing 4-0 home defeat against Oxford United on Saturday; Russell Martin is already under pressure after just one win in their first five games.
articles.body:
Now? They sit 17th in League One, the lowest position in the club's history since they entered the Football League in 1894.

Russell Martin has led the Foxes to just one win in their first five games, and on Saturday they were battered 4-0 at home by Oxford United.

Leicester fans were chanting 'you're getting sacked in the morning' at Martin at the King Power Stadium, who would have been desperate for a good start to turn his reputation around after a dismal end to his time at Southampton, and then a gruelling spell at Rangers.

But can he turn it around? Former Leicester City assistant manager Michael Appleton believes he can.

"It's a difficult moment, there's no doubt about it," Appleton told The EFL Show on Sky Sports News .

"Russell Martin is a very experienced guy now. It was always going to be a difficult job, with big expectations from a club that not too long ago was playing in the Premier League and winning the Premier League.

"With those expectations, you've got to deliver. It's still very early, but losing 4-0 at home, along with the results against Plymouth and Burton, makes it a very difficult start. They've got to start winning games very quickly to address it.

"What I would say is that he's got experience. He's been here before, at a big club with expectations in the league they were in, and he didn't get off to the start he wanted.

"He'll draw on those experiences and maybe use them behind the scenes with the players and staff, speaking about how they dealt with those situations and trying to keep everyone calm.

"It's still very early and there are some good games coming up for them. I always say that when you're in a difficult moment and you're losing games, it feels much worse when you're at home. I'm not saying losing 4-0 at Oxford would have been a good result in any stretch of the imagination, but when it happens at home, it feels so much worse.

"There's a big expectation to deal with, but I think he's more than comfortable doing it."

Meanwhile, Reading co-CEO Joe Jacobson believes the inexperience in the squad is hurting their progress this season.

"They've got a really young team at the minute," he said. "You look at the players they're bringing off the bench and they're taking off experienced players and bringing on younger ones.

"It's difficult for those young players, who will feel the pressure and feel the atmosphere in the stadium. The fans are waiting to turn because of what's happened over the last couple of years. It takes a long time for a fan base to turn and get right behind their team again.

"They have a really tough job on their hands and Russell Martin will know that. He knows exactly what he wants to do and how he wants his team to play. Sometimes that causes division within the fan base, but I'm sure he'll be knuckling down on exactly what he wants to do with his team.

"It reminds me of when he was at Southampton. They lost four games in a row in September and then didn't lose a league match until February. If he can turn the ship, he might start to get a tune out of some of those players."

Jacobson also feels that the disconnect between the club and the fans is also causing an issue, especially since the owners announced Leicester was up for sale, having had a similar recent experience at Reading.

"It's been difficult at Reading because of what happened previously with the ownership there. We've felt it as well. It has taken a long time to get the fans to buy into what you want to do, and the ownership have done amazing things there over the years," he added.

"But when they recently came out and talked about wanting to sell the club and actively looking for a buyer, straight away the fans almost say, 'Well, you don't care now. You just want out. That's your main focus.'

"If the ownership are openly saying they want to sell, it's really difficult for the fans to buy into that. But I still think they're going to have a really successful season.

"Once these players get time on the training field with the manager, I'm sure they'll come good. At the minute, there's that anxiousness and a divided fan base. They want to support their club, but they also want to feel that everyone is pulling in the right direction."

Next up for Martin and Leicester is a trip to Stockport County on Saturday, who are currently sat third in League One.

A decade ago, the Hatters were in National League North. Now they welcome the Foxes to Edgeley Park as favourites for victory.

articles.title: Mbappé se postula para el Balón de Oro: "¿Por quién voto? Por mí"
articles.standfirst: El francés defiende su candidatura en una entrevista con France Football en la antesala del anuncio de los nominados
articles.summary: El francés defiende su candidatura en una entrevista con France Football en la antesala del anuncio de los nominados
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé no piensa esconderse en la carrera por el Balón de Oro. En un avance de la entrevista que France Football emitirá próximamente, y en una jornada en la que también compareció en rueda de prensa, el delantero del Real Madrid reivindicó con firmeza su candidatura al galardón que se entregará el 26 de octubre en Londres. "Tengo la idea de que puedo ganarlo este año, así que no he tomado distancia respecto a eso", afirmó el francés, dejando claro que el premio sigue siendo uno de sus grandes objetivos "a corto plazo". El de Bondy sustentó su defensa en el carácter individual del trofeo, saliendo al paso de quienes le reprochan no haber conquistado títulos colectivos el pasado curso. "Es un premio individual. Se mira lo que ha hecho el jugador de manera individual", razonó. "La gente dice que no he ganado trofeos, pero nunca he visto un Balón de Oro por unanimidad que lo cumpliera todo cada vez. No sé si alguien ha ganado alguna vez con el 100% de los votos. Eso significa que siempre hay alguien que considera que no lo merecía". Su gran argumento, como no podía ser de otro modo, es su Mundial. Mbappé cerró el torneo como máximo goleador de la cita y se llevó la Bota de Oro, un registro que esgrime con orgullo. "Ser el máximo goleador de la historia de la Copa del Mundo, pasar por delante de todas las grandes leyendas de la historia del deporte en el torneo más importante que existe, es algo que quema la retina, un acontecimiento mundial", proclamó. "Terminar como máximo goleador de las competiciones más importantes, donde juegan los mejores del mundo, es algo importante. La historia siempre debe ser recompensada". El delantero, eso sí, no cayó en la soberbia y admitió que respeta otras opiniones. "¿Por quién voto yo? Por mí", reconoció con firmeza. "Pero puedo entender a quienes votan de otra manera, no estamos en la dictadura del pensamiento. Cuando miro los argumentos, cuando miro la competencia, me digo que no sería un robo", zanjó, convencido de que su nombre merece figurar en lo más alto. Las palabras de Mbappé llegan en un momento clave, pues este martes France Football anuncia la lista de los 30 nominados de la edición número 70 del premio, en un curso sin favorito claro. El periodo de evaluación abarca hasta el 19 de julio, día en que España se proclamó campeona del mundo ante Argentina, con Rodri reconocido como mejor jugador del torneo, lo que convierte al centrocampista en uno de los grandes rivales del francés en la puja. La candidatura del galo, sin embargo, arrastra un lastre evidente: la ausencia de títulos de relumbrón. Ni con el Real Madrid, que cerró un curso sin grandes alegrías, ni con una Francia que no levantó el Mundial, pudo Mbappé acompañar sus grandes registros individuales de un entorchado colectivo de peso. Un factor que la historia reciente del galardón suele penalizar, y que competirá con la abrumadora estadística goleadora que el delantero pone sobre la mesa.

articles.title: Calendario de Champions League 2026 - 27: cuándo empieza la fase de liga, partidos y cuándo es la final
articles.standfirst: El formato se mantiene respecto de las dos temporadas anteriores
articles.summary: El formato se mantiene respecto de las dos temporadas anteriores
articles.body: La UEFA Champions League 2026/27 arrancará su 72.ª edición histórica (la 35.ª bajo el nombre de Liga de Campeones y la tercera estrenando la fase de liga). El torneo echó a andar el 7 de julio de 2026 con la clasificación previa y bajará el telón el 5 de junio de 2027 con la gran final en el Estadio Metropolitano de Madrid. El formato se mantiene respecto de las dos temporadas anteriores. Los 36 clubes estarán reunidos en una única tabla y cada uno disputará ocho partidos contra ocho adversarios diferentes: cuatro como local y cuatro como visitante. Los ocho mejores clasificarán directamente a octavos de final, mientras que los ubicados entre el noveno y el vigesimocuarto puesto deberán disputar los playoffs de la fase eliminatoria. Los equipos que finalicen del puesto 25 al 36 quedarán eliminados. La primera jornada de la fase liga tendrá una particularidad: se desarrollará durante tres días, del 8 al 10 de septiembre. El resto de las fechas se disputará principalmente entre martes y miércoles. Martes 8 de septiembre Miércoles 9 de septiembre Jueves 10 de septiembre El Estadio Metropolitano albergará por segunda vez el partido decisivo el sábado 5 de junio de 2027. En 2019, la casa del Atlético de Madrid presenció el triunfo del Liverpool frente al Tottenham (2-0) para alzarse con su sexta corona europea. Con esta cita, Madrid albergará por sexta ocasión la final de la máxima competición continental, solo superada por Londres en número de finales albergadas.

articles.title: Ashley Williams and Alan Sheehan join Wales coaching staff
articles.summary: Ex-Wales captain Ashley Williams and former Swansea boss Alan Sheehan join Craig Bellamy's backroom staff before Wales' Nations League campaign.
articles.body:
Former Wales captain Ashley Williams and ex-Swansea boss Alan Sheehan have joined Craig Bellamy's backroom staff as assistant coaches before Wales' Nations League campaign.

Williams, 42, played 86 times for Wales and skippered the side during their memorable run to the Euro 2016 semi-final.

The former central defender, a Uefa A Licence holder, has recently been involved in coaching at several Wales age group camps but this is his first senior role.

Sheehan, 39, was sacked as head coach of Swansea in November 2025, the former Republic of Ireland youth international having previously been an assistant coach at Swansea, Southampton and Luton Town.

Rodon out for up to 10 weeks with hamstring injury

Lawlor set to miss Wales' Nations League games

The appointments follow James Rowberry stepping down from his role on the Wales coaching staff because of commitments with Championship side Stoke City.

Dutchman Piet Cremers also left his role in Bellamy's backroom staff in July to become the new head coach at Club NXT, Club Brugge's youth academy side.

Former Wales international Andrew Crofts remains in his role as assistant coach following his recent appointment at Tottenham Hotspur.

Wales kick-off their Nations League A campaign in Portugal on Thursday, 24 September before facing Denmark in Copenhagen on Sunday, 27 September.

Bellamy, who was in talks to take the Burnley job in August, is scheduled to announce his squad on Tuesday, 15 September.

articles.title: Davide Ancelotti: "Pellegrini no siempre tiene el reconocimiento que merece, su trayectoria es increíble"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Lille, rival del Betis mañana en la Champions, elogia al técnico chileno
articles.summary: El técnico del Lille, rival del Betis mañana en la Champions, elogia al técnico chileno
articles.body: El entrenador del Lille, Davide Ancelotti, elogió este lunes al técnico del Betis, el chileno Manuel Pellegrini, y advirtió de la experiencia del equipo español, al que recibirá este martes en la primera fecha de la fase de liga de la Champions League. "Manuel Pellegrini, no siempre tiene el reconocimiento que merece, porque tiene una trayectoria increíble y ha tenido mucho éxito", dijo. "Quienes estamos empezando, como yo, le tenemos mucha admiración. No sé si llegaré a su edad. Me digo a mí mismo que es imposible. Pero cuando veo a mi padre (Carlo Ancelotti, seleccionador de Brasil, con 67 años) que tampoco se detiene, tal vez cambie de opinión", señaló Davide, de 37 años, por los 72 del Ingeniero. El entrenador italiano del Lille definió al Betis como un equipo muy organizado y difícil de batir y destacó su experiencia, a pesar de que no jugaba la Champions desde hace 21 años: "El Betis es un equipo organizado, siempre muy difícil de enfrentar, y que, al margen del partido en Levante, no ha encajado muchos goles porque cuenta también con una buena organización defensiva". Expresó, asimismo, la importancia de este torneo para dar un paso adelante en su carrera en solitario, alejado de la sombra de su padre. "La Liga de Campeones es para mí un comienzo en este rol, con otra responsabilidad, pero no un descubrimiento. La experiencia que he vivido como segundo entrenador intento transmitírsela al club y a los jugadores. Espero ahora escribir mi historia en esta competición, con mi nombre de pila".

articles.title: ‘Direction Potocari’: From Srebrenica genocide to a Belgrade football match
articles.summary: Red Star fans honoured convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic. Analysts say that’s nothing new – and that’s the problem.
articles.body:
“Pravac Potocari” or “Direction Potocari” were the words used by former Bosnian Serb general Ratko Mladic as he entered Srebrenica on July 11, 1995.

Mladic was referring to the nearby village of Potocari, which hosted a United Nations peacekeeping base and was the initial gathering point for Bosniak refugees during the war in Bosnia. Under Mladic’s command, Bosnian Serb forces committed a genocide against thousands of Bosniak men and boys in the days that followed.

“Pravac Potocari” was also the slogan the fans of the Serbian football team Red Star chose on Sunday to honour the so-called “butcher of Bosnia”, who died in The Hague, the Netherlands, on August 27, while ⁠serving a life sentence for ‌genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity. During a match against city rivals Partizan in the Serbian capital, the supporters also unveiled a giant image of Mladic and observed a minute of silence in his memory.

The tribute came days after European football governing body UEFA fined Red Star a total of 98,250 euros, or $114,100, over a banner -“General, eternal glory and thanks” – dedicated to Mladic that was unveiled by the club’s ultras during a Europa League playoff away leg in Plzen, in the Czech Republic.

The penalty included a ban on Red Star supporters travelling to the club’s next two European away fixtures, in Lugano, Switzerland on October 15 and Ghent, Belgium on November 26.

It was not the first time Red Star supporters had expressed support for Mladic during a European match. Nine years earlier, fans displayed similar messages during a Europa League tie against Belarusian club BATE Borisov.

‘Most shameful event this stadium has seen’

For Slobodan Georgiev, a news director at TV Nova S in Serbia, the minute of silence at Belgrade’s Marakana stadium marked a qualitative shift rather than a repeat performance.

“Glorifying a convicted war criminal is nothing new, but officially paying tribute to him with a minute of silence is new – and it’s the most shameful event this stadium has witnessed,” Georgiev said. “Displaying the shameful slogan ‘Pravac Potocari’ cannot be justified, though in the coming days we’ll surely see attempts to do so.”

He placed the display in a much longer lineage. “Since the breakup of Yugoslavia, the terraces have served as a recruitment centre for paramilitary formations, and in various forms that haven’t changed to this day,” he said. “The worst messages have always travelled through the terraces – everything the authorities didn’t dare say themselves, they most often said through the stands, as they did … at the Red Star–Partizan match.”

But what made Sunday’s so-called “eternal derby” notable was not only the Red Star display.

Partizan’s own hardcore supporters, the Grobari, had raised their own banner in tribute to Mladic – reading “General, thank you” – just a week earlier, on August 31, during a Serbian Super Liga match against OFK Beograd, with Mladic’s flag flying over the north stand for the full 90 minutes.

For Georgiev, the fan groups are not an autonomous phenomenon, but an instrument. “The state, through its secret services and through criminal groups, has always managed these groups and used them for the worst tasks: Mobilisation in war, crime in peacetime, and delivering the ugliest political messages,” he said. “A stand that boasts it was founded by Zeljko Raznatovic Arkan, and that sings in praise of Ratko Mladic without facing any legal consequence for it, speaks for itself.”

Georgiev was referring to Arkan, the Serbian paramilitary leader whose unit committed atrocities during the Yugoslav wars and who, before his assassination in Belgrade in 2000, was closely associated with Red Star’s hardcore fan base, the Delije – a group he is widely reported to have helped organise.

‘Clearest indication issue deeply ingrained’

Sasa Djordevic, a senior analyst at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC), sees the same continuity Georgiev described, tracing it back further still. “The connection between football hooliganism, nationalism and politics in Serbia dates to the late 1980s and became particularly evident during and after the breakup of former Yugoslavia,” he said. “Certain elements of the hooligan scene have since been exploited as a political ‘rent-a-mob,’ and some group leaders have reaped benefits from political protection or business opportunities.”

What worries him most now is not the display itself, but how unremarkable it risks becoming. “Incidents like those that occurred at Marakana last night risk being perceived as routine rather than serious manifestations of hate speech,” he said. “Public debate has nearly vanished, and society seems increasingly desensitised to violence and hate speech in stadiums. When such behaviour starts to feel normal, it may be the clearest indication that the issue has become deeply ingrained.”

Ivana Jeremic, an editor at the Balkan Insight publication, pointed to why sports venues serve that function so well. “Stadiums have long ceased to be merely sporting arenas – they are fertile ground for sending messages that can’t be spoken publicly, or that come wrapped in a softer form,” she said. “Matches involving Partizan, Red Star, and the national team stand out in particular for this.”

The political ties, she argued, are an open secret. “The political connections between the fans leading the stands and those in power are something of a public secret, with a number of documented examples of direct influence. What we hear or see on the terraces could hardly happen without some form of ‘permission’ from the authorities,” Jeremic said. “When it comes to Mladic, we’ve seen a rise in such messages in recent days. Red Star’s fans, as well as the club itself, are currently perceived as a mouthpiece of the government.”

On Thursday, a Serbian government plane carried Mladic’s body from The Hague to Belgrade for burial, where it was received with military honours.

From the terraces to paramilitary structures

Djordevic traced the mechanism behind this convergence to the same period cited by Georgiev. “During the breakup of Yugoslavia, football stadiums became spaces for nationalist mobilisation, and for some young men the step from organised football violence to paramilitary structures was short,” he said. “Hooligan groups since then cultivate loyalty, hierarchy, readiness to use violence and rapid mobilisation to achieve their extremist views that go beyond strictly football supporter beliefs.”

That structure is not unique to Serbia, but it is particularly acute there. GI-TOC’s regional research examined 122 fan groups, identifying 78 as ultras – and found 21 groups combining violent hooliganism with links to extreme politics. “The most problematic situation was in Serbia, followed by Bosnia and Herzegovina,” Djordevic said, while cautioning against overreach. “The term ‘terrorism’ should be used cautiously: The evidence points to particular groups or individuals linked to violent extremism and paramilitary structures, not supporter groups as a whole.”

UEFA’s disciplinary decision detailed the layers of the punishment: A 50,000-euro ($58,000) fine for transmitting a message unfit for a sporting event, an 8,250-euro ($9,580) fine for team misconduct, and the activation of a suspended sanction originally imposed in April 2025 over racist conduct by Red Star fans – a suspended stadium ban now converted into a one-match travelling ban, conditionally extended for a further two years.

But fines on paper, Djordevic said, rarely reach the people who are actually liable. “The problem is that fines imposed on clubs do not necessarily affect those responsible for the incidents,” he said. “If hooligans remain untouched, financial penalties can become simply another cost of doing business rather than a tool for changing behaviour. That does not mean clubs do not care. They respond when sanctions are certain, substantial, and consistently enforced, as seen more clearly in basketball games than in football.”

The gap, he argued, is not a lack of rules. “Serbia already has a solid legal framework,” he said. “The real issue is enforcement. Sanctions need to be applied quickly, consistently and without exceptions, both to clubs and to individuals responsible for violence and hate speech.”

articles.title: El Sevilla tiene prohibido desconectarse
articles.standfirst: Los hispalenses tiran de raza en Cornellá para rescatar un punto en inferioridad numérica
articles.summary: Los hispalenses tiran de raza en Cornellá para rescatar un punto en inferioridad numérica
articles.body: El empate del Sevilla en su visita al Espanyol confirmó su salto de madurez competitiva. Tras jugar casi la mitad del choque en inferioridad numérica debido a la expulsión de Arouna Sangante, volvió a demostrar una enorme capacidad de resistencia, adelantándose incluso en el marcador con un gol del debutante Lucas Stassin. A pesar de que el tanto de Marcos Fernández en el tramo final dejó un sabor agridulce (1-1), este equipo ha ganado carácter, concentración y oficio comparado al del curso pasado. No solo resulta más correoso para sus rivales, sino que encaja mejor los golpes y nunca se desconecta de los partidos. Con los tres últimos fichajes en la lista de convocados (Fofana, Félix Correia y Stassin), Luis García Plaza apostó por mantener el 4-2-3-1 en Cornellá, reforzando el centro del campo con Guridi en la zona de enganche. Las principales novedades en el once fueron Kochorashvili y Ejuke, que venían de protagonizar una buena segunda parte frente al Atlético de Madrid y entraron por Peque y Julio Díaz. Además, Sangante regresó al centro de la zaga ocupando el lugar de Andrés Castrín, al que todavía se le nota lejos de su mejor estado de forma. Desde el inicio del encuentro se vieron dos propuestas de fútbol muy similares. Tanto Espanyol como Sevilla intentaban robar en un bloque medio-bajo para lanzar transiciones rápidas por los extremos. Los pericos atacaron más la banda de Suazo, que estuvo muy valiente y combativo en su marcaje a Calatrava, el más incisivo de los primeros compases. Con el paso de los minutos, los hispalenses fueron poco a poco adueñándose de la pelota, pero les costaba transformar el dominio en ocasiones de peligro. Antes de la media hora de juego, García Plaza ordenó que Ejuke y Sierra permutaran sus posiciones, pues apenas habían aparecido hasta entonces. El primero brilló menos que en fechas anteriores, desfondándose en la presión y en las ayudas defensivas, mientras que el segundo estuvo poco inspirado y solo se marchó una vez de su par. Si el Sevilla tiene en el nigeriano una de sus grandes armas, el Espanyol puede decir lo mismo de Dolan, aunque el inglés se topó con un Juan Iglesias muy sobrio. La escasez de espacios fue ralentizando el ritmo ofensivo en ambos conjuntos, que no hallaban los caminos hacia el área rival. Robbie Ure, que vivió su noche más discreta desde que aterrizó en Nervión, estaba demasiado aislado entre los centrales como para poder conectar con sus compañeros. En ese contexto, el cuadro sevillista agravó la necesidad de contar con un centrocampista de mayor clarividencia en tres cuartos de campo. El Sevilla controló el tempo de la primera mitad en buena medida gracias a Lucien Agoumé, uno de sus mejores futbolistas en este arranque liguero. El francés lideró la medular a base de trabajar en la sombra y organizar la circulación del juego. Aparte de ser el único que ofrece último pase, ha aprendido a compensar su falta de velocidad potenciando su lectura táctica, posicionándose para interceptar jugadas y orquestando contragolpes. Fue el sevillista que acaparó más posesión completando 35 pases (81% de acierto), además de sumar dos robos y cuatro intercepciones. Otro de los jugadores destacados del partido sería de nuevo Kike Salas, que continúa reforzando su jerarquía dentro de la plantilla. Junto con un perfil como Sangante, encargado de arriesgar más en la salida de balón y en la anticipación, el canterano siempre mantiene la concentración para salir bien al corte, ejerciendo como el gran baluarte defensivo de principio a fin. Así lo reflejan sus estadísticas, otro día más en la oficina con seis despejes y seis duelos aéreos ganados. El guion del partido no cambió hasta la segunda parte con las polémicas arbitrales. En el minuto 55, Edu Expósito filtró un pase a la espalda de la zaga y Sangante rebañó la bola antes de que Roberto Fernández encarase a Odysseas. El colegiado Sesma Espinosa castigó la acción con tarjeta roja y el VAR no lo llamó a revisión de forma incomprensible. "Después de darle a la pelota, ¿qué hace el jugador? No puede desaparecer", protestaría luego Luis García Plaza, que ya había dado entrada a Fofana y Stassin por Kochorashvili y Ure. El Sevilla se vio obligado a remar en inferioridad por segunda vez en cuatro jornadas. A partir de entonces, el choque entró en una fase de descontrol donde el VAR volvió a ser protagonista, anulando un gol a El Hilali por un fuera de juego posicional muy extraño. García Plaza reestructuró dos veces el equipo: primero metió a Castrín por Ejuke para cerrar con 4-4-1 y luego sustituyó a Guiridi y Sierra por Carmona y Manu Bueno pasando a un 5-3-1. El Sevilla defendió como podía sin renunciar al ataque, intentando aprovechar los metros que concedía un Espanyol muy volcado arriba. En el tramo final, el Sevilla agradeció disponer ya de más recursos y fondo de armario. "Fofana llevaba desde el 1 de febrero sin jugar 90 minutos, pero creo que nos va a dar mucho poderío físico y una traslación de campo buenísima. Lucas creo que se va a entender bien con los demás, incluso en algún momento puede jugar con Isaac o con Robbie, pero lleva pocos entrenos. Y a Félix no lo he podido sacar por la expulsión", explicó García Plaza acerca del estreno de sus últimos refuerzos. Stasin exhibió en pocos minutos su olfato y su habilidad para ser indetectable en zonas de peligro. Tras un saque de banda de Carmona al área del Espanyol, el delantero belga cazó un mal despeje y enganchó una volea para poner el 0-1. Por su parte, Fofana abarcó bastante campo y se multiplicó tanto en defensa como en ataque. El francés aporta músculo a un bloque muy sólido de por sí, un factor que puede resultar decisivo en los momentos en que las piernas flaquean. En pleno asedio local, un desajuste en la marca de Carmona permitió a Marcos Fernández sellar el empate definitivo. "No podemos defender el área así en la última jugada y es un error que tenemos que corregir", lamentó el técnico madrileño. Aun así, el Sevilla demostró que sabe competir y que no desconecta de los partidos, y eso muchas veces tiene premio. Aunque el empate le sepa agridulce, suma un punto muy meritorio que sigue reforzando la confianza del grupo.

articles.title: Adrián bendice el debut en la Champions de Álvaro Valles: "Está mostrando un grandísimo nivel"
articles.standfirst: El exguardameta bético, en la expedición del equipo que viajó este lunes a Lille
articles.summary: El exguardameta bético, en la expedición del equipo que viajó este lunes a Lille
articles.body: A principios de agosto, apenas un par de meses después de anunciar que colgaba los guantes, Adrián San Miguel se incorporó a la estructura de la Dirección Deportiva del Betis para llevar a cabo tareas de coordinación deportiva e institucional. Este martes, en su primer viaje en Champions con el equipo, ha pasado por los micrófonos de la radio oficial del club para analizar cómo afronta la entidad este hito histórico de regresar más de 20 años después a la máxima competición continental. Sobre sus sensaciones y el viaje de la expedición bética: "El discurso del piloto del vuelo ha sido buenísimo y se ha llevado una gran ovación y aplauso de todo el mundo, lo que nos hacía recordar un poco que disfrutemos el camino. El año pasado es verdad que conseguir el hito de clasificarnos para la Champions, fue algo muy bonito, y ahora comenzamos el camino realmente. Yo creo que es un camino para disfrutarlo, para conseguir nuevos hitos, intentar lograr cosas que no se han conseguido hasta ahora en el club, y un camino para competir. Ojalá hagamos un buen papel en esta Champions League". Primer rival, el Lille de Davide Ancelotti: "Pues sí, la verdad es que en las últimas temporadas han dado ese salto de calidad, por así decirlo, y se ha incluido al equipo dentro de los cuatro o cinco primeros de la liga francesa. Es cierto que tienen nuevo entrenador, Davide Ancelotti, que tiene una filosofía bastante peculiar y al que bien conozco también personalmente. Va a ser un partido aguerrido, un partido que nos va a costar hacernos con el balón porque ellos lo tratan también muy bien y les gusta tenerlo. Pelota solo hay una, así que ahí va a haber una gran disputa. Pero estoy seguro de que, con el hambre que tiene este equipo de comenzar bien la Champions y al ver a todos los compañeros tan involucrados desde este principio de temporada, va a ser un partido muy bonito". El rendimiento de Álvaro Valles: "Pues sí, sí que está siendo primordial y un gran protagonista para nosotros. Es verdad que yo siempre digo que cuanto menos protagonista sea el portero, mejor, porque eso quiere decir que el equipo está jugando en campo contrario y el portero pasa desapercibido; pero para eso está el portero también. Álvaro está mostrando un grandísimo nivel, no solo esta temporada, sino que la temporada pasada también lo demostró. Es cierto que al final va a ser una temporada de grandes exigencias, y está demostrando que ahora va a debutar en la Champions, una competición superbonita en la que estoy seguro de que está máximamente ilusionado. Me alegro muchísimo por él, ahí estaremos para apoyarlo y ojalá pueda mantener este nivel toda la temporada, por supuesto". Sus recuerdos de la Champions de hace 21 años: "Pues mira, lo recuerdo en el estadio Benito Villamarín con mi padre; estaba en ese partido contra el Chelsea. Me acuerdo del partido de Anfield también, que creo que hizo gol Sinama-Pongolle, ¿puede ser?. Aquí perdimos 2-1 con gol de Arzu". Jugar de nuevo el torneo: "El partido del Anderlecht también fue un momento histórico para el club. Ahora nos han tocado rivales diferentes: algunos más conocidos, otros no tanto, otros más poderosos, y otros que están creciendo y aspirando a mucho. Va a ser algo muy especial para toda la plantilla poder disputar esta Champions, y para toda la afición también poder acompañar al equipo. Esas noches de Champions en La Cartuja, que esperemos que sean muy especiales, y fuera de casa también estoy seguro de que mañana habrá muchos béticos, y en los siguientes escenarios habrá un desplazamiento masivo de la afición verdiblanca".

articles.title: Marcus Freeman Reveals Halftime Speech to CJ Carr, Notre Dame Players amid Blowout vs. Wisconsin
articles.summary: Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman to set aside all of their preseason expectations when they went into the locker room at halftime of Sunday's win over Wisconsin.
articles.body:
Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman to set aside all of their preseason expectations when they went into the locker room at halftime of Sunday's win over Wisconsin.

The Fighting Irish led by just three before outscoring the Badgers 28-3 in the second half.

"Sometimes, you don't believe it till you're in it," Freeman said, per ESPN's Adam Rittenberg . "Like, I can sit here and tell you, 'You have to struggle to achieve what we achieved tonight,' but until you're in the middle of it, it's hard to understand it. So, I wanted to remind them that at halftime. ... Don't assume the future's going to go in any direction. Just focus on what you have in the moment."

Notre Dame ranked fourth in the preseason AP Top 25. Freeman has built a roster that a lot of people believe is good enough to contend for a national title.

Because of that, some may have been surprised by the 13-10 halftime score. But it's rare that an eventual champion goes wire-to-wire without having some hiccups.

"Outside of our building, there can be a narrative that college football is easy, and we should steamroll teams," Fighting Irish quarterback CJ Carr said. "The reality is that's a really good Wisconsin team with some really good players. So, adjusting and staying consistent throughout the game was really helpful for us."

The Notre Dame defense kept Wisconsin to under 300 yards. Carr went 19-of-29 for 239 yards and two touchdowns. Aneyas Williams carried the ball 20 times for 90 yards and two scores.

The Fighting Irish weren't impressive from start to finish, but they provided some evidence of why they might be the last team standing in January. Their second-half response was the strongest indication.

articles.title: CJ Carr Addresses Narrative Notre Dame 'Should Steamroll Teams' After Blowout vs. Wisconsin
articles.summary: Despite leading No. 4 Notre Dame to an easy 41-13 victory over Wisconsin in Sunday's season opener, quarterback CJ Carr isn't getting too ahead of himself.
articles.body:
Despite leading No. 4 Notre Dame to an easy 41-13 victory over Wisconsin in Sunday's season opener, quarterback CJ Carr isn't getting too ahead of himself.

Carr told reporters after the victory that while these blowouts are expected of the Fighting Irish, he knows they're not the norm, so he's approaching each game with a competitive mindset.

"Outside of our building, there can be a narrative that college football is easy, and we should steamroll teams," Carr said, per ESPN's Adam Rittenberg . "The reality is that's a really good Wisconsin team with some really good players. So, adjusting and staying consistent throughout the game was really helpful for us."

Carr was 19-of-29 for 239 yards and two touchdowns in the victory over the Badgers. He was much more efficient in the second half of the game, completing 10 of 13 passes for 133 yards and a touchdown in what Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman called an "excellent" performance.

Carr admitted that it took until the end of the first half for the offense to get into a rhythm, and the Fighting Irish used that momentum in the second half with touchdown drives of 70, 75 and 88 yards.

"The results showed that we wanted a fight, and that's what we got," Carr said.

Notre Dame will look to continue its dominance when it hosts Rice in Week 2 on Saturday.

articles.title: El Eibar es una trituradora cada vez que abre la lata
articles.standfirst: Encadena 16 triunfos tras empezar el partido por delante en el marcador: sólo ha encajado 3 goles en esos encuentros
articles.summary: El Eibar encadena 16 triunfos tras empezar el partido por delante en el marcador: sólo ha encajado 3 goles en esos encuentros
articles.body: El 7 de diciembre de 2025, la Cultural venció en Ipurua tras remontar el gol inicial de Arbilla y agravó la situación del Eibar. El conjunto armero levantó el vuelo en 2026 para firmar la mejor vuelta de su historia y aquella dolorosa derrota supuso el último encuentro en el que no ha sido capaz de ganar después de adelantarse en el marcador. Abrir la lata es sinónimo de victoria para un equipo fiable cuando toca defender la ventaja. Lo fue con San José y lo continúa siendo con Jokin Aranbarri. Hasta en 16 partidos ha empezado ganando el Eibar desde que perdió contra los leoneses y todos ellos se han resuelto con una victoria para sus intereses. Los últimos 13 partidos de la pasada temporada en los que comenzó mandando en el marcador y los 3 del presente ejercicio han supuesto triunfos que le han disparado en la tabla. Además, en todas esas victorias logró mantener su portería a cero hasta en 13 ocasiones y sólo ha encajado 3 goles en casi 1.500 minutos de juego. Los datos explican lo complicado que es meter mano a este Eibar cuando es capaz de dar el primer puñetazo. La mejor noticia del arranque liguero de los armeros no es su posición en la tabla, sino las similitudes en el juego y las numerosas fortalezas que se encuentran con el equipo que hizo historia en la segunda vuelta del pasado curso. Con Aranbarri, el Eibar sigue siendo un equipo versátil, productivo en fase ofensiva y un muro en las labores de contención. 13 de las 16 veces en las que ha abierto el marcador lo ha hecho en la primera mitad. Atrás han quedado tiempos en los que el sufría cuando tenía que defender una renta favorable en los minutos finales. Ahora es un equipo compacto, que sabe juntar sus líneas y disfrutar también en el estrés que supone tener que conservar un resultado favorable cuando el rival acumula efectivos en ataque. Una mejoría que está ligada a una mayor calidad defensiva en la defensa del área, un mayor sacrifico de los jugadores de ataque, pero que también responde a un cambio de mentalidad en ese tipo de contextos. Hasta en inferioridad numérica, como le ha pasado en las dos últimas jornadas, es un equipo que no se descompone. En Andorra se vio obligado a jugar durante la última media hora con un futbolista menos por la expulsión de Magunazelaia y no concedió demasiadas ocasiones a un rival que acabó desesperado con el cerrojo armero. Tampoco el Granada aprovechó la expulsión de Jair para recortar distancias en el marcador. Aranbarri está sabiendo explotar una de las grandes herencias que dejó San José para mantener la dinámica ganadora que acompaña al equipo en 2026.

articles.title: Marcus Freeman Reacts to Notre Dame RBs Replacing Jeremiyah Love, Jadarian Price in Opening Win
articles.summary: Notre Dame running backs Aneyas Williams and Nolan James Jr. have the unenviable task of replacing first-round picks Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price this season.
articles.body:
Notre Dame running backs Aneyas Williams and Nolan James Jr. have the unenviable task of replacing first-round picks Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price this season.

But after the pair combined to rush for 119 yards and two touchdowns in a season-opening blowout over Wisconsin, 41-19, head coach Marcus Freeman seemed pleased with the performance and realistic about his expectations for the position going forward.

"They showed to be the backs that we expected," he told reporters . "I don't expect to replace J-Love and JD with just one guy or two guys. It's going to be a committee. It's going to be keeping guys fresh and continue to let them run and continue to let them try to wear down the defense."

Williams did most of the heavy lifting on the ground, rushing 20 times for 90 yards and two scores, though Nolan James Jr. was impactful in the passing game, catching four passes for 67 yards and a touchdown.

It was a bit more of a sluggish start for No. 4 Notre Dame, which led just 13-10 over Wisconsin heading into halftime. But the Fighting Irish came out firing in the second half, outscoring their opponents by a 28-3 margin to secure the win.

"Outside of our building, here can be a narrative that college football is easy, and we should steamroll teams," quarterback CJ Carr told reporters. "The reality is that's a really good Wisconsin team with some really good players. So, adjusting and staying consistent throughout the game was really helpful for us."

It was the sort of second-half recovery that made Notre Dame's title aspirations ahead of the 2026 season seem realistic, even if tougher opponents than Wisconsin are yet to come.

"It does a lot for your mentals," Freeman told reporters of the result. "To win with the final score being 41-13 does a lot for the confidence, and it's important to have confidence as you continue to move forward."

articles.title: South Carolina's Nutritionist Gets Game Ball for Helping Players with 'Unforgiving' Weather Elements
articles.summary: South Carolina coach Shane Beamer made a point to shout out the team's nutritionist following a 57-0 blowout of Kent State in Week 1.
articles.body:
South Carolina coach Shane Beamer made a point to shout out the team's nutritionist following a 57-0 blowout of Kent State in Week 1.

Heeding the suggestion of his players, Beamer awarded a game ball to Yimy Queipo Rodriguez, the director of football performance nutrition:

Rodriguez had his work cut out for him this past Saturday in what The Athletic's Christopher Kamrani described as "unforgiving elements never seen before by the program." The heat index at Williams-Brice Stadium approached 110 degrees, the highest ever for a Gamecocks home game.

South Carolina and Kent State agreed to shorten the fourth quarter by five minutes because of the heat.

Beamer commended his team for having "no cramping issues" despite the challenging conditions.

Of course, it helped that South Carolina's opponent was so overmatched. The Gamecocks were up 29 points by halftime and finished with a 645-179 edge in total yards. Beamer had the luxury of emptying the bench midway through the second half.

The heat might've become a bigger factor if this was a tough SEC matchup requiring 60 minutes of full effort.

But that doesn't diminish how well Rodriguez and his staffers did to keep South Carolina's players hydrated. The game ball was well earned.

articles.title: En el jardín de Llorente
articles.standfirst: Marcos regresa a Anfield, el estadio en el que ha marcado dos dobletes. El primero, le coronó como rojiblanco. El segundo llegó hace un año.
articles.summary: Marcos regresa a Anfield, el estadio en el que ha marcado dos dobletes. El primero, le coronó como rojiblanco. El segundo llegó hace un año.
articles.body: Regresa el Atlético a Anfield y con él, un Marcos Llorente que tiene en el césped del histórico estadio su particular jardín. El campo del Liverpool es el escenario en el que cambió la historia del 14 como rojiblanca, el lugar donde empezó a ganarse a la hinchada. La historia empezó un 11 de marzo de 2020 en el que el fútbol, y todo el planeta, se preparaban para la pandemia del coronavirus. Un partido que estuvo en el aire disputarse y en el que Simeone convirtió al mediocentro que había llegado para reemplazar a Rodrigo Hernández en uno de sus grandes puntales ofensivos. Aquella noche en la que Oblak se vistió de Messi (así lo definió el propio Cholo), Llorente jugó en punta y firmó dos tantos fundamentales para tumbar al que entonces era el mejor equipo de Europa (defendía corona de la Champions... ganada precisamente en el Metropolitano). Su doblete y el gol de Morata colocaron un 2-3 en el marcador que dio el pase al Atlético a cuartos de final del torneo. Nacía la leyenda del Llorente ofensivo que fue determinante meses después para ganar la segunda Liga con Simeone. No contento con eso, Llorente repitió visita y actuación hace un año. El Liverpool empezó arrasando y dos tantos tantos suyos colocaron el empate (ganaron los locales con un gol de Virgil van Dijk en el añadido). Cuatro tantos en dos partidos para convertir Anfield en su estadio 'preferido' más allá del Metropolitano. Eso sí, el 14 (noticia la última semana por anunciar su retirada voluntaria de la selección con la que ganó el Mundial) regresa a un estadio del que se marchó dolido hace un año pese a su doblete: "Duele, no es fácil remontar un 2-0 en Anfield", comentó minutos después de salir de su jardín.
